rationale: The packet ties the proposal to the authoritative incident's excessive capacity removal, multi-subsystem blast radius, slower-removal remediation, and minimum-capacity safeguard, so source support passes. Contract fairness fails because the public input gives a removal count but defines neither the valid server-index set nor how an indexed server affects subsystem counts; it also does not specify the capacity.remove return schema or duplicate/rejected-index behavior. Those missing terms are necessary to choose legal batches, predict whether issuing a call itself violates the safety obligation, and report exactly the host-accepted indexes. The task remains natural, the host-owned immutable ledger isolates the structural witness, the capacity-floor mechanism is distinct from the listed novelty families, and the proposed reference/mutant/malformed/replay probe has explicit falsifiers. The closest competing verdict is promote if one assumes indexes are 0 through removeCount-1, each target-cell removal decrements every subsystem listing that cell, and a precise facade response; those assumptions are not stated, so contract terms cannot be filled in by the reader.
